en.headline: Wang Fuk Court fire marks first anniversary as community holds memorials
en.dek: One year after the blaze that killed 168 people at the Tai Po estate, religious groups are holding memorial services while the government has said it will not organise an official ceremony but will not obstruct lawful…
body: Today marks the first anniversary of the Wang Fuk Court fire in Tai Po, which broke out on 26 November last year and killed 168 people, including domestic helpers, making it Hong Kong’s deadliest fire in decades.

The government has said it will not hold an official memorial event. Chief Secretary Eric Chan stated earlier that various community activities were already planned and that authorities would not prevent lawful commemorations, while warning against any acts intended to disrupt public order.

Catholic and other religious groups have held or are holding memorial masses and services. The Support Fund for affected residents has reached about HK$4.8 billion, and authorities have announced additional grants for flat owners and families of the deceased. Police and other agencies have brought multiple prosecutions related to the renovation project and fire safety.

The Independent Committee’s report found partial responsibility with several government departments. Systemic reforms, including amendments to multiple ordinances, are under way. Many former residents remain in temporary housing as the estate’s towers stay vacant.

zh.headline: 宏福苑火災一周年 社區舉行悼念活動
zh.dek: 大埔宏福苑火災今日滿一周年，造成168人死亡。政府表示不會舉辦官方悼念儀式，但不會阻止合法悼念活動，多個宗教團體已舉行追思彌撒。
body: 今日是大埔宏福苑五級火災發生一周年。火災於去年11月26日爆發，造成168人死亡，包括外籍家庭傭工，是香港數十年來最嚴重的火災之一。
政府早前表示不會舉辦官方悼念活動。政務司司長陳國基指出，社區已有多項悼念安排，當局不會阻止合法悼念，但會依法處理任何意圖破壞社會秩序的行為。
天主教香港教區及其他宗教團體已舉行或正舉行追思彌撒及悼念儀式。政府設立的援助基金已達約48億元，並公布向業主及罹難者家屬提供額外資助。警方及其他部門已就相關工程及消防安全提出多項檢控。
獨立委員會報告指多個政府部門須承擔部分責任。相關系統性改革及多項條例修訂正在進行。不少前居民仍暫居過渡房屋，宏福苑樓宇目前仍然空置。
